newsitem.title: UK: Med oil products mostly up, cold boosts gas oil $5.
newsitem.headline: Med oil products mostly up, cold boosts gas oil $5.

text.p: Med oil products were mostly firmer on Monday as cold weather heralded stronger demand for heat and power, traders said.
Gas oil firmed $5.50 with futures and on stronger demand triggered by colder weather across Europe. But the Med remains quiet with the only marked demand for Algerian low sulphur.

Russians were assessed at around high cif quotes flat basis Genoa. Traders reported availability of Russians but said they suspected bad weather at Tuapse could lead to some delays. A low sulphur diesel traded at a discount to high cif quotes basis Genoa for delivery January 1-5.
The Asian arb is marginal and attention focused on India's tender for one percent sulphur high speed diesel for February.

Naphtha held steady in quiet activity. Traders said the underlying market was looking fairly long but there was little downward pressure on prices with sellers reluctant to offer cargoes in to the current void of demand.
Sellers were pegged at around $217-$218 a tonne cif Med with nearest bids around $4 under this level.
Gasoline was also steady in thin trade with a good deal of first half January programs already completed leaving buyers relaxed for the near term at least.
Premium unleaded cargoes were valued around $221.50 a tonne cif Med.
High sulphur cracked fuel oil markets were slightly firmer and swaps were heard bid up at $115.50 fob Med by the end of the day. But activity was thin.
Low sulphur markets were steady to firmer, with swaps at around $124/$125 fob NWE. No new business was heard done since last week's physical trades at $124 and $125 fob Scandinavia.
